label: CONCRETE_6: having esse in re: HasEsseInRe InAct esse x:= InAct x esse: the candidate has its own…
term: concrete: having esse in re (adopted sense)
definition: HasEsseInRe InAct esse x := InAct x esse: the candidate has its own act of existence in reality, read with the shared Aquinas vocabulary (DEF-ESSE) as being in the first sense of De ente c.1, which posits something in re. Being in the second sense (the truth of a proposition, in which privations 'are') does not count, and neither does a nature's esse in the soul (De ente c.2). Concreteness is NOT defined by causal power, spatial location or materiality. What esse in re further requires is left to downstream metaphysical questions.
note: The owner's adopted sense (#1103, 2026-11-06): 'in thomistic terms we can say that concrete things have esse, and abstract things do not have them'. Aquinas does not use the modern word 'concrete'; identifying the modern contrast with having esse in re is the owner's stipulation. The Aquinas distinctions it draws on are the claims AQUINAS-DE-ENTE-C1-ENS-DUPLICITER, AQUINAS-DE-ENTE-C2-NATURE-DUPLEX-ESSE and AQUINAS-ST-I-Q85-A1-AD2-MATHEMATICALS-ABSTRACTED. Owner decision on #1103 (2026-11-06): https://github.com/moritzbrantner/truth-core/issues/1103#issuecomment-6683616439. See docs/notes/concrete-abstract.md. Reuse check: DISAMB-BEING already separates being as entity (DEF-BEING-AS-ENTITY, the respect esse) from being as the truth of a proposition (DEF-BEING-AS-TRUTH-OF-A-PROPOSITION) and rules out counting a privation as in act with respect to esse; HasEsseInRe is InAct x esse in the first of these senses.
